security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG decoder or translator allows RV32-only double-wide instructions (PADD.DB/DH/DW/DBS/DHS/DWS using OP-IMM-32 major opcode 0x1b) to execute in RV64 mode, or allows RV64-only PADD.W to execute in RV32 mode. The double-wide variants use 4-bit register-pair fields (rd_p/rs1_p/rs2_p) that encode even-register pairs via index*2; if executed on RV64, the XLEN-dependent element iteration count doubles (XLEN/8=8 on RV64 vs 4 on RV32), causing reads/writes beyond intended element boundaries within each register, and the register-pair scheme designed for 32-bit registers misapplies to 64-bit register pairs.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: translate.c or insn32.decode: OP-IMM-32 (0x1b) or OP-32 (0x3b) opcode decoding for P-extension packed-add instructions lacking XLEN mode guard (check_xlen or REQUIRE_RV32/REQUIRE_RV64), or 4-bit register-pair field extraction (rd_p/rs1_p) without x0 special-case and even-register enforcement
security_spec.summary: P-extension packed-add instructions have strict RV32/RV64 availability constraints and use 4-bit register-pair encodings; QEMU must trap illegal-mode executions and correctly handle register-pair x0 aliasing, otherwise cross-element data corruption occurs due to wrong XLEN-dependent iteration bounds
